messages.subject: problems with annotation file directory path
parts:
Dear all,
I am new to aroma.affymetrix and I have problems putting the annotation files in the correct directory. I have created chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6 and put the three necessary files into it.  R is in the correct working directory, but the program is still not able to find the CDF files (see below)

It is probably something very simple, but what am I doing wrong?

Best wishes,

Ingo

messages.subject: Re: problems with annotation file directory path
parts:
Looks like you are missing one level of subdirectory structure for the
CDF files. The CDF files needs to be in a subdirectory (from the
working directory) called annotationData/chipTypes/..., not just
chipTypes.

Hope this helps.

Dong

Hi,
It's not clear to me from your email what your directory structure IS,
but here is a help page I made to give a quick visual guide (and
hopefully has no errors!):

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/quick-summary-of-required-file-structure

By the way, your working directory and appropriate subdirectories can be
anywhere (in case 'C:/Programme/R/R-2.6.1/library/aroma.affymetrix'
isn't really where you'd prefer); it's only the relationship of the
subdirectories to the working directory that must be fixed.

Best,
Elizabeth

Hi Ingo,
Is you folder named

annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6

or

annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWide_6?


The folder name must be the same as the cdf file name.

What is the full name of your cdf file? Is it
"GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf"? (that is what your code indicates). If so,
try instead

> AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType ("GenomeWideSNP_6,Full")

Maybe it's a problem with the 'tags=' option.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] problems with annotation file directory path
parts:
Ok, here is how to troubleshoot (assuming you are not using Windows
Shortcut links):

library(aroma.affymetrix)
stopifnot(isDirectory("annotationData"))
stopifnot(isDirectory("annotationData/chipTypes"))
stopifnot(isDirectory("annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/"))
stopifnot(isFile("annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf"))

That should tell you were the error/typo is.

/Henrik

Let me guess: Windows was set to hide filename extensions, correct?
This is such a classical problem that cause problems in so many
different areas. We had another incidence like this in March 2007.
See thread "AffymetrixCdfFile problem with link"
[http://tinyurl.com/3an3hj], and especially the conclusion of the last
message in that thread. I cannot really understand why they (read
Microsoft) decided that, by default, users must be "protected" from
those poor three letters at the end of every file.

Good that it works for you now.

/Henrik
